He gave an example of one Michigan-based contract manufacturer that, until it started working with Bloom, was taking on odd jobs like refurbishing Nest thermostats and Bird scooters, or working with Chick-fil-A displays.
That same company is now bidding on drone assembly contracts.

passages: Margaret Hamilton, the computer pioneer whose software powered the first moon landing, has died, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) announced on Wednesday.
In 1969, minutes before the Apollo 11 spacecraft was set to make history by landing on the lunar surface, an onboard computer’s alarm rang, indicating an emergency.
“Our astronauts didn’t have much time, but thankfully they had Margaret Hamilton,” he said.
She continued to perfect the craft in an MIT laboratory, writing software that could detect enemy aircraft.
When the institute received a Nasa contract to develop the Apollo onboard flight software, she jumped at the opportunity.
In an era before titles such as software engineer and computer scientist became mainstream, Hamilton, who died on 30 September, learned to program under the tutelage of a renowned MIT meteorologist.
MIT computer scientist led development of software for moon mission and earned Presidential Medal of Freedom
The software was working just as Hamilton and her team intended.

When the institute received a Nasa contract to develop the Apollo onboard flight software, she jumped at the opportunity. “I was attracted both by the sheer idea and the fact that it had never been done before. I was the first programmer to join and the first woman they hired,” she told the Guardian in 2019. In 1969, minutes before the Apollo 11 spacecraft was set to make history by landing on the lunar surface, an onboard computer’s alarm rang, indicating an emergency. Faced with a decision of whether to abort the mission, the spacecraft continued on. The software was working just as Hamilton and her team intended. “It quickly became clear the software was not only informing everyone that there was a hardware-related problem but was compensating for it – restarting and re-establishing the highest priority tasks. Hamilton is survived by her daughter, a son-in-law, two grandsons and four great grandchildren, according to MIT. Reflecting on the mission, in a 2009 interview with MIT News, Hamilton said: “Looking back, we were the luckiest people in the world; there was no choice but to be pioneers; no time to be beginners.”

sources.title: Microsoft event debuts new AI-friendly hardware and Windows changes
passages: In its first live event in two years, Microsoft today announced its newest Surface laptop, outlined a host of changes coming to Windows 11, and shared a vision of how local-AI and agentic workflows could reshape personal computing for those in the dev community as well as home enthusiasts.
OS builds featured on the Surface Ultra and Spark Box will arrive with an updated Windows software suite to support local model testing out of the box.

Bringing all of this new agentic workflow together with traditional Windows is a concept that Microsoft calls “Hybrid Intelligence,” which is a move away from cloud-backed AI solutions and a move toward local ones.
Joined on stage by Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, President of Windows and Devices Pavan Davuluri also unveiled the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box.
With 128GB of unified memory and the onboard Nvidia RTX GPU, the box claims one petaflop (that’s 1,000 teraflops) of AI compute performance.

Microsoft is betting big on local AI with the changes announced today, but questions about security and user acceptance still remain, especially in light of their past missteps and other recent AI agent mishaps .
Originally teased in May 2026 , the new Surface Laptop Ultra will be Microsoft’s first offering to take advantage of the new Nvidia RTX Spark SoC (system on a chip).
It will begin shipping on October 16 and is available for pre-order now.
The unit physically resembles something like an Android TV box or game console more than it does a traditional PC.
Microsoft’s baked-in Windows AI, Copilot, is getting a major overhaul.
The new Copilot layout will see things divided into three tabs:
Coming to a Windows PC later this year, the new update will allow Windows users to execute system-level tasks directly from the search bar.

For those who might still feel a little trepidation about turning over their entire digital lives and files to AI bots, Microsoft announced the availability of Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), a security framework designed to keep agent activities confined to a sandbox.

Available to developers today, the framework allows system admins and organizations to monitor active agents working within their systems and to specifically set guardrails for each, ensuring control over exactly what each agent is able to access.
Get ready for more AI in your Windows and more AI on the desktop.

extraction.body: Get ready for more AI in your Windows and more AI on the desktop. In its first live event in two years, Microsoft today announced its newest Surface laptop, outlined a host of changes coming to Windows 11, and shared a vision of how local-AI and agentic workflows could reshape personal computing for those in the dev community as well as home enthusiasts. Originally teased in May 2026 , the new Surface Laptop Ultra will be Microsoft’s first offering to take advantage of the new Nvidia RTX Spark SoC (system on a chip). The device has a starting price of $2,599, and comes in various SoC and memory configurations, with either a 5120-core or 6144-core Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB of LPDDR5x unified memory. It will begin shipping on October 16 and is available for pre-order now. While the new Ultra is clearly focused on the developer crowd, graphical performance was highlighted during the presentation to show off just how capable the laptop can be. By leaning on unified memory allocation rather than the physical VRAM limits of a traditional GPU, the laptop can assign its resources to handle modern gaming tasks as well as local AI development and deployment. The new Gears of War: E-Day was shown running on the system, meaning that even without a traditional gaming GPU, AAA titles are on the table. Joined on stage by Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, President of Windows and Devices Pavan Davuluri also unveiled the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box. This is a $5,999 anodized aluminum black box “designed to meet the needs of frontier developers.” The Spark Dev Box ships with a custom “developer-optimized” build of Windows 11 pre-configured for AI development and local AI use. With 128GB of unified memory and the onboard Nvidia RTX GPU, the box claims one petaflop (that’s 1,000 teraflops) of AI compute performance. The RTX Spark Dev Box’s design is quite sleek. The unit physically resembles something like an Android TV box or game console more than it does a traditional PC. In fact, the vent pattern on the top of the unit is reminiscent of what you see looking down at the top of an Xbox Series X. According to Microsoft’s provided press materials, the venting on the RTX Spark Dev box has 1,000 chassis air vents as a nod to the 1,000 teraflops of AI performance. Outside of the hardware announcements, Microsoft outlined a host of changes headed for Windows 11 this fall. OS builds featured on the Surface Ultra and Spark Box will arrive with an updated Windows software suite to support local model testing out of the box. Microsoft’s baked-in Windows AI, Copilot, is getting a major overhaul. The new Copilot layout will see things divided into three tabs: Coming to a Windows PC later this year, the new update will allow Windows users to execute system-level tasks directly from the search bar. Rather than opening up something like Control Panel to adjust display settings, the user will presumably be able to describe the action they want and have the system execute it directly from the taskbar tray. For those who might still feel a little trepidation about turning over their entire digital lives and files to AI bots, Microsoft announced the availability of Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), a security framework designed to keep agent activities confined to a sandbox. Available to developers today, the framework allows system admins and organizations to monitor active agents working within their systems and to specifically set guardrails for each, ensuring control over exactly what each agent is able to access. MXC acts as a policy layer that directs compute traffic to the appropriate isolation backend. Depending on the workload, MXC can shift to a process container, session container, WSL container, or even an experimental hardware-backed isolation called MicroVM. Bringing all of this new agentic workflow together with traditional Windows is a concept that Microsoft calls “Hybrid Intelligence,” which is a move away from cloud-backed AI solutions and a move toward local ones. Hybrid Intelligence will allow Surface Laptop Ultra or RTX Spark Dev Box users to allocate memory as they see fit for any specific application, as well as offer native support for local frameworks like llama.cpp and models from the Deepseek and Nvidia Nemotron families. Microsoft is betting big on local AI with the changes announced today, but questions about security and user acceptance still remain, especially in light of their past missteps and other recent AI agent mishaps . The Surface Laptop Ultra hits shelves next week—keep an eye out for our review, and we’ll try to figure out whether it’s worth the $2,599 entry price and what this local AI capability buys you. After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

extraction.body: Get ready for more AI in your Windows and more AI on the desktop. In its first live event in two years, Microsoft today announced its newest Surface laptop, outlined a host of changes coming to Windows 11, and shared a vision of how local-AI and agentic workflows could reshape personal computing for those in the dev community as well as home enthusiasts. Originally teased in May 2026 , the new Surface Laptop Ultra will be Microsoft’s first offering to take advantage of the new Nvidia RTX Spark SoC (system on a chip). The device has a starting price of $2,599, and comes in various SoC and memory configurations, with either a 5120-core or 6144-core Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB of LPDDR5x unified memory. It will begin shipping on October 16 and is available for pre-order now. While the new Ultra is clearly focused on the developer crowd, graphical performance was highlighted during the presentation to show off just how capable the laptop can be. By leaning on unified memory allocation rather than the physical VRAM limits of a traditional GPU, the laptop can assign its resources to handle modern gaming tasks as well as local AI development and deployment. The new Gears of War: E-Day was shown running on the system, meaning that even without a traditional gaming GPU, AAA titles are on the table. Joined on stage by Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, President of Windows and Devices Pavan Davuluri also unveiled the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box. This is a $5,999 anodized aluminum black box “designed to meet the needs of frontier developers.” The Spark Dev Box ships with a custom “developer-optimized” build of Windows 11 pre-configured for AI development and local AI use. With 128GB of unified memory and the onboard Nvidia RTX GPU, the box claims one petaflop (that’s 1,000 teraflops) of AI compute performance. The RTX Spark Dev Box’s design is quite sleek. The unit physically resembles something like an Android TV box or game console more than it does a traditional PC. In fact, the vent pattern on the top of the unit is reminiscent of what you see looking down at the top of an Xbox Series X. According to Microsoft’s provided press materials, the venting on the RTX Spark Dev box has 1,000 chassis air vents as a nod to the 1,000 teraflops of AI performance. Outside of the hardware announcements, Microsoft outlined a host of changes headed for Windows 11 this fall. OS builds featured on the Surface Ultra and Spark Box will arrive with an updated Windows software suite to support local model testing out of the box. Microsoft’s baked-in Windows AI, Copilot, is getting a major overhaul. The new Copilot layout will see things divided into three tabs: Coming to a Windows PC later this year, the new update will allow Windows users to execute system-level tasks directly from the search bar. Rather than opening up something like Control Panel to adjust display settings, the user will presumably be able to describe the action they want and have the system execute it directly from the taskbar tray. For those who might still feel a little trepidation about turning over their entire digital lives and files to AI bots, Microsoft announced the availability of Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), a security framework designed to keep agent activities confined to a sandbox. Available to developers today, the framework allows system admins and organizations to monitor active agents working within their systems and to specifically set guardrails for each, ensuring control over exactly what each agent is able to access. MXC acts as a policy layer that directs compute traffic to the appropriate isolation backend. Depending on the workload, MXC can shift to a process container, session container, WSL container, or even an experimental hardware-backed isolation called MicroVM. Bringing all of this new agentic workflow together with traditional Windows is a concept that Microsoft calls “Hybrid Intelligence,” which is a move away from cloud-backed AI solutions and a move toward local ones. Hybrid Intelligence will allow Surface Laptop Ultra or RTX Spark Dev Box users to allocate memory as they see fit for any specific application, as well as offer native support for local frameworks like llama.cpp and models from the Deepseek and Nvidia Nemotron families. Microsoft is betting big on local AI with the changes announced today, but questions about security and user acceptance still remain, especially in light of their past missteps and other recent AI agent mishaps . The Surface Laptop Ultra hits shelves next week—keep an eye out for our review, and we’ll try to figure out whether it’s worth the $2,599 entry price and what this local AI capability buys you. After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

The device has a starting price of $2,599, and comes in various SoC and memory configurations, with either a 5120-core or 6144-core Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB of LPDDR5x unified memory. It will begin shipping on October 16 and is available for pre-order now.

While the new Ultra is clearly focused on the developer crowd, graphical performance was highlighted during the presentation to show off just how capable the laptop can be. By leaning on unified memory allocation rather than the physical VRAM limits of a traditional GPU, the laptop can assign its resources to handle modern gaming tasks as well as local AI development and deployment. The new Gears of War: E-Day was shown running on the system, meaning that even without a traditional gaming GPU, AAA titles are on the table.

Joined on stage by Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, President of Windows and Devices Pavan Davuluri also unveiled the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box. This is a $5,999 anodized aluminum black box “designed to meet the needs of frontier developers.” The Spark Dev Box ships with a custom “developer-optimized” build of Windows 11 pre-configured for AI development and local AI use. With 128GB of unified memory and the onboard Nvidia RTX GPU, the box claims one petaflop (that’s 1,000 teraflops) of AI compute performance.

The RTX Spark Dev Box’s design is quite sleek. The unit physically resembles something like an Android TV box or game console more than it does a traditional PC. In fact, the vent pattern on the top of the unit is reminiscent of what you see looking down at the top of an Xbox Series X. According to Microsoft’s provided press materials, the venting on the RTX Spark Dev box has 1,000 chassis air vents as a nod to the 1,000 teraflops of AI performance.

Outside of the hardware announcements, Microsoft outlined a host of changes headed for Windows 11 this fall. OS builds featured on the Surface Ultra and Spark Box will arrive with an updated Windows software suite to support local model testing out of the box.
Microsoft’s baked-in Windows AI, Copilot, is getting a major overhaul. The new Copilot layout will see things divided into three tabs:

Coming to a Windows PC later this year, the new update will allow Windows users to execute system-level tasks directly from the search bar. Rather than opening up something like Control Panel to adjust display settings, the user will presumably be able to describe the action they want and have the system execute it directly from the taskbar tray.

For those who might still feel a little trepidation about turning over their entire digital lives and files to AI bots, Microsoft announced the availability of Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), a security framework designed to keep agent activities confined to a sandbox. Available to developers today, the framework allows system admins and organizations to monitor active agents working within their systems and to specifically set guardrails for each, ensuring control over exactly what each agent is able to access.

MXC acts as a policy layer that directs compute traffic to the appropriate isolation backend. Depending on the workload, MXC can shift to a process container, session container, WSL container, or even an experimental hardware-backed isolation called MicroVM.

Bringing all of this new agentic workflow together with traditional Windows is a concept that Microsoft calls “Hybrid Intelligence,” which is a move away from cloud-backed AI solutions and a move toward local ones. Hybrid Intelligence will allow Surface Laptop Ultra or RTX Spark Dev Box users to allocate memory as they see fit for any specific application, as well as offer native support for local frameworks like llama.cpp and models from the Deepseek and Nvidia Nemotron families.

Microsoft is betting big on local AI with the changes announced today, but questions about security and user acceptance still remain, especially in light of their past missteps and other recent AI agent mishaps . The Surface Laptop Ultra hits shelves next week—keep an eye out for our review, and we’ll try to figure out whether it’s worth the $2,599 entry price and what this local AI capability buys you.
